summary: A serverless Azure portfolio with analytics and Gemini-powered analysis.
roleSummary: Cloud architecture, AI integration & automated deployment
contribution: Built and extended an Azure application with serverless APIs, persistence, identity, telemetry, file workflows, and a Gemini-powered assistant routed through the backend.

decisions.title: Learn the cloud service boundaries
decisions.reason: Static Web Apps, Functions, Cosmos DB, and Entra ID provided practical experience connecting hosting, compute, data, and identity.

decisions.title: Keep Gemini behind the API boundary
decisions.reason: The Vue client sends chat, portfolio statistics, and uploaded document text to an Azure Function; only the backend reads the Gemini API key and calls Gemini.

decisions.title: Reassess the operational cost
decisions.reason: The Azure architecture was useful for learning, but the requirements of this portfolio fit a simpler self-hosted deployment.

lesson: A cloud architecture study covering CI/CD, observability, and a secure backend boundary for third-party AI, followed by a deliberate move to simpler hosting for this portfolio.
name: Serverless Portfolio Hub
purpose: Build a serverless Azure application to explore cloud deployment, identity, observability, and CI/CD in practice. After meeting the original assignment requirements, I extended it with file workflows and a lightweight Gemini-powered assistant that could discuss portfolio statistics and analyze uploaded document text. The Vue client routes AI requests through .NET Azure Functions, keeping the Gemini API key in backend environment configuration.

media.alt: Serverless Portfolio Hub deployment architecture from GitHub Actions to Azure services
media.title: Deployment architecture

coreStory: I built Serverless Portfolio Hub as an assignment to explore cloud deployment, identity, observability and CI/CD in practice. After meeting the requirements, I extended it with file workflows and a Gemini-powered assistant for portfolio statistics and uploaded document text.

I connected the Vue frontend to .NET Azure Functions, keeping the Gemini API key in the backend. The project remains a cloud architecture study; its operational complexity helped me choose simpler hosting for this portfolio.
